_readme: What AI coding tools and model labs publish about instruction files, which model runs each job, effort settings and context. Every claim is one plain sentence plus a quote of at most 25 words copied verbatim from source_url, with the date it was checked. tier "tool" = the coding tool's own docs; tier "lab" = the model maker's own docs about its own models. scripts/check-sources.mjs re-fetches every source_url and fails if a quote is no longer on the page; scripts/validate-data.mjs checks the shape. role_defaults names a model for a helper job only where the tool's own docs name that job; every other job runs on the same model as the lead (inherit). model_refs maps the strings a tool's config accepts (for example "sonnet") to catalog ids in data/models.json. effort_pages links each lab's own page on effort or reasoning settings. Nothing in this file ranks models against each other.

claims.sentence: Claude Code loads ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md as user instructions that apply to every project on that machine.
claims.quote: Personal preferences for all projects

claims.sentence: Claude Code reads project instructions from ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md, shared with a team through source control.
claims.quote: Team-shared instructions for the project

claims.sentence: Claude Code reads a CLAUDE.local.md at the project root for private per-project instructions that stay out of version control.
claims.quote: For private per-project preferences that shouldn't be checked into version control

claims.sentence: Claude Code joins every CLAUDE.md file it finds into one context instead of letting one file replace another.
claims.quote: All discovered files are concatenated into context rather than overriding each other.

claims.sentence: A CLAUDE.md file can pull in another file with an @path import line.
claims.quote: CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using @path/to/import syntax.

claims.sentence: A relative @path import in CLAUDE.md resolves from the folder of the file that contains it.
claims.quote: Relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory.

claims.sentence: CLAUDE.md imports can nest, up to four levels deep.
claims.quote: Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of four hops.

claims.sentence: By default, Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when there is no CLAUDE.md in the working directory or any folder above it.
claims.quote: By default, Claude reads AGENTS.md only when you have no CLAUDE.md in your working directory or above it.

claims.sentence: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md on its own starting with version 2.1.277.
claims.quote: Reading AGENTS.md directly requires Claude Code v2.1.277 or later.

claims.sentence: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, a managed CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/ files do not stop Claude Code from reading AGENTS.md; they load alongside it.
claims.quote: Don't count, and keep loading alongside AGENTS.md

claims.sentence: Adding a CLAUDE.local.md to a project that relies on AGENTS.md stops Claude Code from reading that AGENTS.md under the default setting.
claims.quote: adding one to keep your own uncommitted instructions in a project that relies on AGENTS.md stops Claude from reading AGENTS.md for you.

claims.sentence: An @AGENTS.md import line in a CLAUDE.md next to AGENTS.md lets Claude Code and other coding tools share one instruction file.
claims.quote: you can still keep it as the one file every tool shares by putting an @AGENTS.md import in a CLAUDE.md next to it.

claims.sentence: Keeping an @AGENTS.md import in CLAUDE.md does not make Claude Code read AGENTS.md twice.
claims.quote: Keeping the import never makes Claude read AGENTS.md twice, whichever Project instructions value you use.

claims.sentence: Claude Code loads every .md file under a project .claude/rules/ folder, including subfolders.
claims.quote: All .md files are discovered recursively

claims.sentence: A rule file can limit itself to matching files with a paths field in its YAML frontmatter.
claims.quote: Rules can be scoped to specific files using YAML frontmatter with the paths field.

claims.sentence: A rule file with no paths field loads every session and applies to all files.
claims.quote: Rules without a paths field are loaded unconditionally and apply to all files.

claims.sentence: Rule files in ~/.claude/rules/ apply to every project on the machine.
claims.quote: Personal rules in ~/.claude/rules/ apply to every project on your machine.

claims.sentence: Claude Code docs set a target of under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file, saying longer files use more context and reduce adherence.
claims.quote: target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence.

claims.sentence: Files pulled in through CLAUDE.md imports still load into the context window at launch.
claims.quote: imported files still load and enter the context window at launch

claims.quote: Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!

claims.sentence: Claude Code cost docs advise keeping CLAUDE.md under 200 lines of essentials.
claims.quote: Aim to keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines by including only essentials.

claims.sentence: Claude Code loads skills only when they are invoked, so instructions moved from CLAUDE.md into skills stay out of the base context.
claims.quote: Skills load on-demand only when invoked, so moving specialized instructions into skills keeps your base context smaller.

claims.sentence: Claude Code docs state that model performance degrades as the context window fills.
claims.quote: Claude's context window fills up fast, and performance degrades as it fills.

claims.sentence: Each Claude Code subagent runs in its own context window with its own system prompt, tools and permissions.
claims.quote: Each subagent runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions.

claims.sentence: Subagent requests count toward the same usage limits as the main Claude Code conversation.
claims.quote: It also sends its own requests, which count toward the same usage limits as your main conversation.

claims.sentence: Claude Code cost docs say to hand verbose work such as test runs to subagents so only a summary returns to the main conversation.
claims.quote: Delegate these to subagents so the verbose output stays in the subagent's context while only a summary returns to your main conversation.

claims.sentence: Claude Code docs state agent teams use about 7x the tokens of a standard session when teammates run in plan mode.
claims.quote: Agent teams use approximately 7x more tokens than standard sessions when teammates run in plan mode

claims.sentence: Claude Code reads subagent definition files from .claude/agents/ (project) and ~/.claude/agents/ (user), including subfolders.
claims.quote: Claude Code scans .claude/agents/ and ~/.claude/agents/ recursively

claims.sentence: When two subagent files share a name, Claude Code uses the higher-priority location, and project .claude/agents/ ranks above user ~/.claude/agents/ in its table.
claims.quote: When multiple subagents share the same name, Claude Code uses the one from the higher-priority location.

claims.sentence: A Claude Code subagent file needs only name and description in its frontmatter; tools and model are optional.
claims.quote: Only name and description are required.

claims.sentence: The model field in a subagent file accepts sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, a full model ID, or inherit.
claims.quote: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, a full model ID such as `claude-opus-5-5`, or `inherit`

claims.sentence: Claude Code resolves a subagent's model from the per-call model parameter, then the file model field, then CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, then the main conversation model.
claims.quote: Claude Code resolves the subagent's model in this order:

claims.quote: If you set both variables, subagents run on the model in `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`.

claims.sentence: The model key in a Claude Code settings file sets the model each new session starts on.
claims.quote: Set the model every new session uses, so you don't have to pick one with /model each time.

claims.sentence: Claude Code takes the model from /model, then --model, then ANTHROPIC_MODEL, then the settings model field, in that priority order.
claims.quote: configure permanently in your settings file using the model field

claims.sentence: Claude Code applies .claude/settings.local.json over the committed .claude/settings.json for the same key.
claims.quote: Claude Code applies that file over the committed .claude/settings.json

claims.sentence: ~/.claude/settings.json holds user settings for every project and sits last in Claude Code settings precedence.
claims.quote: your personal settings for every project.

claims.sentence: When several settings files set the same list key, Claude Code merges the lists rather than keeping only one.
claims.quote: Claude Code combines the lists instead of picking one, so each file can add entries without removing another file's.

claims.sentence: The opusplan model setting uses opus in plan mode and switches to sonnet for execution.
claims.quote: Special mode that uses opus during plan mode, then switches to sonnet for execution

claims.sentence: A model field in a skill file switches the model for the rest of that turn without saving it to settings.
claims.quote: Model to use when this skill is active. The override applies for the rest of the current turn and isn't saved to settings.

claims.sentence: The effortLevel settings key sets a default effort level for models with no saved level.
claims.quote: Set a default effort level for models you haven't saved a level for.

claims.sentence: Claude Code resolves session effort from an explicit choice first, then saved settings, then the model default.
claims.quote: Claude Code resolves the session's effort level in this order, taking the first that applies:

claims.sentence: In Claude Code, Opus 5.5 starts at medium effort unless a setting or explicit choice sets another level.
claims.quote: Opus 5.5 starts at medium unless one of the sources above sets a level for it

claims.sentence: The effort levels Claude Code offers depend on the model in use.
claims.quote: The available effort levels depend on the model.

claims.sentence: If a chosen effort level is not supported by the model, Claude Code uses the highest supported level at or below it.
claims.quote: Claude Code falls back to the highest supported level at or below the one you set.

claims.sentence: The maxEffortLevel settings key caps the effort level a session can use.
claims.quote: Cap the effort level a session can use, leaving lower levels available.

claims.sentence: An effort field in a subagent file overrides the session effort level while that subagent runs.
claims.quote: Effort level when this subagent is active. Overrides the session effort level.

claims.sentence: An effort field in a skill file overrides the session effort level while that skill runs.
claims.quote: Effort level when this skill is active. Overrides the session effort level.

claims.sentence: Since v2.1.198 the built-in Explore subagent inherits the main conversation model instead of always running on Haiku.
claims.quote: As of v2.1.198, Explore inherits the main conversation's model instead of always running on Haiku.

claims.sentence: On the Claude API, the Explore subagent model is capped at Opus.
claims.quote: inherits from the main conversation, capped at Opus on the Claude API

claims.quote: define one with model: haiku to keep exploration on a lower-cost model

claims.sentence: The built-in Explore and Plan subagents do not load CLAUDE.md files.
claims.quote: Explore and Plan skip your CLAUDE.md files and the git status snapshot to keep research fast and inexpensive.

claims.sentence: Claude Code subagent docs list routing tasks to Haiku as one way to control costs.
claims.quote: Control costs by routing tasks to faster, cheaper models like Haiku

claims.sentence: Claude Code cost docs say to set model: haiku in the subagent file for simple subagent tasks.
claims.quote: For simple subagent tasks, specify model: haiku in your subagent configuration

claims.sentence: A subagent that inherits the session model follows a /model switch; a model field in its file keeps it fixed.
claims.quote: To keep a custom subagent on a smaller model, set model in its definition.

claims.sentence: Claude Code cost docs say to use Sonnet for agent-team teammates.
claims.quote: Use Sonnet for teammates. It balances capability and cost for coordination tasks.

claims.sentence: Claude Code cost docs say Sonnet handles most coding tasks and costs less than Opus, with Opus kept for complex architecture or multi-step reasoning.
claims.quote: Sonnet handles most coding tasks well and costs less than Opus. Reserve Opus for complex architectural decisions or multi-step reasoning.

claims.sentence: Claude Code describes its sonnet alias as the latest Sonnet model for daily coding tasks.
claims.quote: Uses the latest Sonnet model for daily coding tasks

claims.sentence: Claude Code describes its opus alias as the latest Opus model for complex reasoning tasks.
claims.quote: Uses the latest Opus model for complex reasoning tasks

claims.sentence: Claude Code describes its haiku alias as the Haiku model for simple tasks.
claims.quote: Uses the fast and efficient Haiku model for simple tasks

claims.quote: the fable alias resolves to Fable 5.1, except in Claude apps gateway sessions

claims.sentence: Claude Code's model-config table shows the opus alias resolving to Opus 5.5 and the sonnet alias to Sonnet 5 on the Anthropic API; other providers resolve to other versions.

claims.sentence: Codex reads AGENTS.md files before it starts any task.
claims.quote: Codex reads AGENTS.md files before doing any work.

claims.sentence: At global scope Codex reads AGENTS.override.md from its home directory (~/.codex unless CODEX_HOME is set) if it exists, and AGENTS.md otherwise.
claims.quote: In your Codex home directory (defaults to `~/.codex`, unless you set `CODEX_HOME`), Codex reads `AGENTS.override.md` if it exists.

claims.sentence: From the project root down to the working directory, Codex checks each directory for AGENTS.override.md, then AGENTS.md, then any names listed in project_doc_fallback_filenames, and includes at most one file per directory.
claims.quote: In each directory along the path, it checks for `AGENTS.override.md`, then `AGENTS.md`, then any fallback names in `project_doc_fallback_filenames`.

claims.sentence: Codex joins the instruction files it finds from the root down, so files nearer the working directory appear later in the combined prompt.
claims.quote: Codex concatenates files from the root down, joining them with blank lines.

claims.sentence: Codex stops adding instruction files once their combined size reaches project_doc_max_bytes, which is 32 KiB by default.
claims.quote: stops adding files once the combined size reaches the limit defined by project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB by default)

claims.sentence: Codex sets its default model for the CLI and IDE with the model key in config.toml.
claims.quote: Choose the model Codex uses by default in the CLI and IDE. model = "gpt-6-sol"

claims.sentence: Codex sets reasoning effort with the model_reasoning_effort key in config.toml, applied when the model supports it.
claims.quote: Tune how much reasoning effort the model applies when supported. model_reasoning_effort = "medium"

claims.sentence: A project's .codex/config.toml outranks the user's ~/.codex/config.toml, is read from the project root down with the closest file winning, and loads only for trusted projects.
claims.quote: Project config files: `.codex/config.toml`, ordered from the project root down to your current working directory (closest wins; trusted projects only)

claims.sentence: A Codex profile is a separate file, ~/.codex/<name>.config.toml, layered over config.toml when Codex runs with --profile <name>.
claims.quote: When you pass `--profile profile-name`, Codex loads `~/.codex/config.toml`, then overlays `~/.codex/profile-name.config.toml`.

claims.sentence: From Codex 0.134.0, --profile no longer reads [profiles.<name>] tables inside config.toml.
claims.quote: In Codex 0.134.0 and later, --profile no longer reads [profiles.profile-name] from config.toml

claims.sentence: A Codex subagent with no model or reasoning effort configured uses the parent agent's model and effort.
claims.quote: If you don't configure a subagent model or `model_reasoning_effort`, the subagent inherits the parent agent's model and reasoning effort.

claims.sentence: The agents.default_subagent_model key in config.toml sets the default model for agents that Codex spawns.
claims.quote: agents.default_subagent_model string No Set the default model for spawned agents.

claims.sentence: Codex custom agents are standalone TOML files in ~/.codex/agents/ (personal) or .codex/agents/ (project).
claims.quote: add standalone TOML files under ~/.codex/agents/ for personal agents or .codex/agents/ for project-scoped agents.

claims.sentence: A model or model_reasoning_effort set inside a Codex custom agent file takes precedence for that agent.
claims.quote: If a custom agent file sets `model` or `model_reasoning_effort`, the value in the file takes precedence.

claims.sentence: Cursor project rules are .mdc files stored in .cursor/rules.
claims.quote: Project rules live in .cursor/rules as .mdc files and are version-controlled.

claims.sentence: Cursor ignores plain .md files in .cursor/rules; project rules need the .mdc extension.
claims.quote: Project rules must use the .mdc extension.

claims.sentence: Cursor decides when to include a rule from three frontmatter fields: description, globs and alwaysApply.
claims.quote: Under the hood, the three frontmatter fields interact to determine when a rule is included

claims.sentence: Cursor reads AGENTS.md in the project root and in subdirectories.
claims.quote: Cursor supports AGENTS.md in the project root and subdirectories.

claims.sentence: Cursor User Rules are set in the app's Customize > Rules screen and apply across all projects.
claims.quote: User Rules are global preferences defined in Customize → Rules that apply across all projects.

claims.sentence: Cursor merges Team, Project and User Rules in that order, with earlier sources taking precedence on conflict.
claims.quote: Rules are applied in this order: Team Rules → Project Rules → User Rules

claims.sentence: Cursor's rules guide says to keep each rule under 500 lines.

claims.quote: The model field controls which model a subagent uses.

claims.sentence: A Cursor subagent uses the parent agent's model by default (model: inherit).
claims.quote: Uses the same model as the parent agent. This is the default.

claims.sentence: In a Cursor subagent's model field, options in square brackets after the model ID set reasoning effort, speed and context window.
claims.quote: Append square brackets to a model ID to set per-model options like speed, reasoning effort, and context window.

claims.sentence: Cursor subagents are markdown files in .cursor/agents/ (project) or ~/.cursor/agents/ (user).
